how_to_apply: Visit the official MP ESB website (www.esb.mp.gov.in) or the MP Online portal (www.mponline.gov.in).
Under Citizen Services, select the ESB link and read the online application instructions and exam rules carefully.
Fill the online application form between 21.08.2026 and 04.09.2026, entering all required academic and service-related details accurately - an incomplete application cannot be submitted.
Upload a colour photograph, signature, and handwriting sample as per the specified format, along with the required declaration text in your own handwriting.
Upload your original appointment order, along with your school's DISE Code and (for government school teachers) your Unique ID/IFMIS Code.
Pay the exam fee of ₹1,000 per paper, plus the applicable MP Online portal fee, via credit/debit card, net banking, or an authorized MP Online kiosk.
Use the correction window (21.08.2026 to 09.09.2026) to fix any errors in the submitted application, on payment of the prescribed correction fee where applicable.
Download the admit card (Test Admit Card/T.A.C.) from the Board's website closer to the exam date.
important_instructions: Aadhaar registration is mandatory for all candidates; multi-level biometric verification is mandatory at the time of exam entry and during the exam, and Aadhaar must be unlocked at the time of verification. Candidates must carry an original photo identity proof (Voter ID, PAN Card, Aadhaar Card, Driving Licence, or Passport) to the exam centre; e-Aadhaar is valid only if verified through UIDAI. Candidates will be allowed entry into the exam room only until the specified reporting time; late candidates will not be granted entry. Use of electronic devices such as mobile phones, calculators, log tables, digital watches, sunglasses, and any unfair-means material is strictly prohibited in the exam room. Candidates must bring a black ball-point pen and their downloaded admit card to the exam hall. No candidate will be permitted to leave the exam room between the start and end of the exam. Facilities such as a scribe (writer) or compensatory time are available for eligible visually impaired, upper-limb-disabled, cerebral palsy, and certain other specified categories of candidates, subject to prior application to the Board at least 10 days before the exam with supporting documents and an affidavit. This exam's eligibility/result is valid only for the continued service eligibility of existing in-service teachers and is NOT valid for future direct recruitment to government teacher posts. Re-totalling/re-evaluation of the result is not permitted once declared by the Board. Any query regarding the application can be directed to the MP Online Helpdesk (0755-6720200) or the candidate can contact the toll-free number 1800-233-7899, or email complaints to [email protected].

content_sections.heading: MP ESB TET 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Candidates should note the following dates for the application, correction, and exam process. The exam will be conducted in two shifts. In the first shift, candidates report between 8:00 AM and 9:00 AM, important instructions are read from 9:50 AM to 10:00 AM (10 minutes), and the exam runs from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM (2 hours 30 minutes). In the second shift, candidates report between 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM, instructions are read from 2:50 PM to 3:00 PM, and the exam runs from 3:00 PM to 5:30 PM.

content_sections.heading: MP ESB TET 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: This exam is open only to in-service (currently employed) teachers - it is not a recruitment exam and is not open to fresh candidates seeking a new government teaching job. All in-service primary-level teachers in government schools - Sahayak Shikshak (Assistant Teacher), Prathmik Shikshak, Sahayak Adhyapak, Samvida Shala Shikshak Varg 3 (Contract School Teacher Class 3), Prayogshala Sahayak (Laboratory Assistant), Prathmik Shikshak Vigyan, and Sahayak Shikshak Vigyan - who have not cleared the eligibility test prescribed under the Right to Education Act are eligible to appear. In-service teachers at the primary level in non-government schools who have not cleared TET may also appear. All in-service secondary-level teachers in government schools - Shikshak, Madhyamik Shikshak, Adhyapak, and Samvida Shala Shikshak Varg 2 (Contract School Teacher Class 2) - who have not cleared the eligibility test prescribed under the Right to Education Act are eligible to appear. In-service teachers at the secondary level in non-government schools who have not cleared TET may also appear. Candidates applying for this exam must currently be serving in the post for which they are appearing in the eligibility test. This eligibility test's result will not be valid for appointment through direct recruitment to a government teacher post in future.

content_sections.heading: MP ESB TET 2026 Exam Pattern
content_sections.text: Both the Primary and Secondary Teacher Eligibility Tests are conducted as a single online (computer-based), objective-type (MCQ) paper of 150 marks, with a duration of 2 hours 30 minutes and no negative marking. Language-1 questions are based on proficiency in the language chosen by the candidate in the application form. Language-2 must be different from Language-1, and candidates can choose from Hindi, English, Sanskrit, and Urdu. The question paper level and content are based on the topics of the prevalent Madhya Pradesh Class 1–5 syllabus/textbooks, though the difficulty level and linkage may extend up to high-school standard. The paper has two parts. Part A is compulsory for all candidates. Part B (120 marks) requires the candidate to choose one subject from the seven listed, matching the main subject of their graduation degree. Note: The content of Part A (General Knowledge, Reasoning & Numerical Ability, Pedagogy) is set at a level equivalent to a Higher Secondary school student, while the Hindi and English language content is set at the Higher Secondary School exam level. Part B content is set at graduate level; questions are based on the prevalent Madhya Pradesh Class 9 and 10 syllabus topics, though the difficulty level and linkage are of graduate standard, with a focus on concept understanding, problem-solving, and pedagogy.

content_sections.text: The detailed syllabus is set out separately for each subject and paper in the rule book. Key syllabus areas include: Child Development & Pedagogy (Primary): concept of child development, Piaget/Pavlov/Kohler/Thorndike theories, child-centred and progressive education, concept and measurement of intelligence, personality, inclusive education, understanding children with special needs, learning and pedagogy, cognition and emotion, motivation, memory and forgetting. Languages (Hindi, English, Sanskrit, Urdu): unseen passage comprehension, grammar, pedagogy of language development including principles of language teaching, listening/speaking/reading/writing skills, teaching-learning materials. Mathematics (Primary): number system, place value, four basic operations, fractions, geometry basics, measurement, patterns; plus pedagogical issues like development of logical thinking through mathematics teaching, evaluation methods. Environmental Study (Primary): family and community, plants and animals, natural resources, food, water and air pollution, disaster management, space science, plus pedagogical issues of environmental education. Mathematics/Science/Social Science/Language subjects (Secondary, Part B): based on the content areas of the Madhya Pradesh Class 9–10 syllabus, set at graduate-level difficulty with pedagogy of the respective subject. Given the length and detail of the full syllabus (covering multiple subjects across both Primary and Secondary levels), candidates are advised to refer to the complete syllabus chapters in the official rule book for topic-by-topic preparation.

faq.question: Q1. What is the MP ESB Teacher Eligibility Test 2026?
faq.answer: It is a special eligibility test conducted by MP ESB exclusively for currently in-service primary and secondary school teachers who have not yet cleared TET, following a Supreme Court order dated 01.09.2025.

faq.question: Q2. Who can apply for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: Only in-service (currently employed) government and non-government school teachers at the primary or secondary level who have not previously cleared TET are eligible. It is not open to fresh candidates seeking new recruitment.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: The online application closes on 04.09.2026. A correction window remains open until 09.09.2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the exam date for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: The exam is scheduled to begin from 12.10.2026 (Monday), conducted in two shifts per day.

faq.question: Q5. What is the application fee for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: The exam fee is ₹1,000 per paper for all candidates, regardless of category, plus an MP Online portal fee of ₹60 (kiosk) or ₹20 (registered login).

faq.question: Q6. What is the exam pattern for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: Both the Primary and Secondary Teacher Eligibility Tests are a single 150-mark MCQ paper of 2 hours 30 minutes, with no negative marking. The Secondary test has a compulsory Part A (30 marks) and a subject-choice Part B (120 marks).

faq.question: Q7. What are the qualifying marks for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: General/Unreserved candidates need 60% marks; SC/ST/OBC/Divyangjan/EWS candidates need 50% marks to qualify.

faq.question: Q8. Is the MP ESB TET 2026 result valid for new government teacher recruitment?
faq.answer: No. This exam's eligibility/result is valid only for the continued service eligibility of existing in-service teachers and will not be recognized for future direct recruitment to government teacher posts.

faq.question: Q9. How can I apply online for MP ESB TET 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible in-service teachers can apply online at www.esb.mp.gov.in or via the MP Online portal between 21.08.2026 and 04.09.2026, uploading their appointment order, DISE Code, and other required details.

faq.question: Q10. By when must in-service teachers qualify TET as per the Supreme Court order?
faq.answer: In-service teachers recruited before the RTE Act, with more than 5 years of service remaining, must qualify TET by 31st August 2028. Teachers with less than 5 years of service left may continue without qualifying TET, but cannot be considered for promotion without it.
